uss_missouri.name: USS Missouri (BB-63)
uss_missouri.fun_fact: The Japanese surrender ending WWII was signed on her deck on September 2, 1945. She's now a museum ship at Pearl Harbor.

uss_enterprise_cv6.name: USS Enterprise (CV-6)
uss_enterprise_cv6.fun_fact: The most decorated U.S. Navy ship of WWII. She participated in more major actions against Japan than any other ship.

uss_arizona.name: USS Arizona (BB-39)
uss_arizona.fun_fact: Sunk during the attack on Pearl Harbor. 1,177 crew members lost their lives. The memorial now stands over her resting place.
uss_arizona.special_note: In honor of those who gave all. This ship is unlocked by default.

uss_iowa.name: USS Iowa (BB-61)
uss_iowa.fun_fact: Served as President Roosevelt's transportation to the Tehran Conference in 1943. Now a museum ship in Los Angeles.

uss_new_jersey.name: USS New Jersey (BB-62)
uss_new_jersey.fun_fact: The most decorated battleship in U.S. Navy history. Served in WWII, Korea, Vietnam, and Lebanon.

uss_yorktown_cv5.name: USS Yorktown (CV-5)
uss_yorktown_cv5.fun_fact: Played a crucial role at the Battle of Midway despite being damaged. Sunk during the battle but helped turn the tide of the Pacific War.

uss_hornet.name: USS Hornet (CV-8)
uss_hornet.fun_fact: Launched the Doolittle Raid on Tokyo in April 1942 - the first air raid to strike the Japanese home islands.

uss_lexington.name: USS Lexington (CV-2)
uss_lexington.fun_fact: One of the first large aircraft carriers. Lost at the Battle of the Coral Sea in May 1942.

uss_fletcher.name: USS Fletcher (DD-445)
uss_fletcher.fun_fact: Lead ship of the most numerous class of destroyers ever built. 175 Fletcher-class destroyers served in WWII.

uss_sullivans.name: USS The Sullivans (DD-537)
uss_sullivans.fun_fact: Named after the five Sullivan brothers who died together when USS Juneau was sunk. Now a museum ship in Buffalo, NY.

uss_indianapolis.name: USS Indianapolis (CA-35)
uss_indianapolis.fun_fact: Delivered components for the first atomic bomb to Tinian. Sunk by Japanese submarine four days later; only 316 of 1,195 crew survived.

pt_109.name: PT-109
pt_109.armament: Four torpedo tubes, various machine guns
pt_109.fun_fact: Commanded by Lieutenant John F. Kennedy. Sunk by Japanese destroyer in 1943; Kennedy's heroism saved his crew.

uss_nautilus.name: USS Nautilus (SSN-571)
uss_nautilus.fun_fact: The world's first operational nuclear-powered submarine. First vessel to complete a submerged transit of the North Pole.

f4u_corsair.name: F4U Corsair
f4u_corsair.armament: Six .50 caliber machine guns, up to 2,000 lbs bombs
f4u_corsair.fun_fact: Achieved an 11:1 kill ratio against Japanese aircraft. Its bent gull-wing design is instantly recognizable.

f6f_hellcat.name: F6F Hellcat
f6f_hellcat.fun_fact: Destroyed 5,223 aircraft during WWII - more than any other Allied naval aircraft. Designed specifically to counter the Zero.

sbd_dauntless.name: SBD Dauntless
sbd_dauntless.armament: Two .50 caliber machine guns, up to 2,250 lbs bombs
sbd_dauntless.fun_fact: Sank more enemy shipping than any other Allied aircraft. Decisive in the Battle of Midway, sinking four Japanese carriers.
